[BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) distinguishes masked-item reconstruction, using bidirectional context, from next-item prediction, using history plus an appended mask. Protocol implication: withholding an interaction from a diagnostic input does not undo its inclusion in parameter training. Prefix accuracy on such interactions measures in-sample recovery, compatible with memorization; it neither establishes next-item generalization nor proves memorization alone. Remove the target occurrence and all later context, append the reserved mask, and read its representation. This prevents direct input leakage but cannot remove training exposure. Genuine held-out evidence comes from the benchmark’s existing validation interactions, excluded from training; keep its split unchanged.

Repeated item identity differs from repeated exposure to the target event. A held-out future interaction can legitimately repeat an earlier item: [RepeatNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.02646) explicitly distinguishes repeat targets from exploration targets. Recommended diagnostic reporting: separate training-exposed target events from held-out validation events, then stratify each by whether the target item appears in the prefix; include subgroup counts. Preserve legitimate earlier occurrences. Strong repeat-target performance can reflect useful repeat prediction, while strong recovery of training events remains insufficient evidence of generalization.

For auxiliary sampled-ranking diagnostics, include the positive exactly once; sample unique negatives excluding that positive, padding/mask tokens, and known positives under the declared diagnostic policy, using only permitted data. Excluding prefix items from negatives must not remove a repeated positive. Record exclusions and candidate counts; keep the host’s 99-negative policy, seed, and macro validation HR@10 unchanged. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons relative to full-catalog metrics: interpret these results strictly within their candidate protocol.
